title: Real workflows: .NET and Docker
summary: needs, artifacts, a .NET build-and-test workflow and a Docker build-and-push workflow.

steps.title: needs: jobs that wait
body: Jobs run **in parallel** by default. `needs` makes a job wait for others and skip if any of them failed:
lint (runs alone, in parallel with build)
The jobs form a **DAG** (directed acyclic graph). A cycle (`a` needs `b`, `b` needs `a`) is rejected before anything runs.

steps.prompt: `build` and `lint` start together. `lint` fails; `build` succeeds. `test` needs `build`; `docker` needs `[test, lint]`. What is `docker`'s result?
steps.explain: A job is skipped when any job in its `needs` failed, unless it overrides that with `if: always()` or `if: failure()`.

steps.title: A .NET build-and-test workflow
body: - run: dotnet test --no-build -c Release --logger trx --results-directory TestResults
if: always()                 # upload results even when tests fail
- run: dotnet publish src/Api -c Release -o out --no-build
Restore once, build once, test the build you made, publish the build you tested.

steps.prompt: Why is `if: always()` on the *test results* upload step?
options: When `dotnet test` fails, later steps are skipped by default, and failing runs are exactly when you need the report
So the artifact is never deleted
Because artifacts cannot be uploaded from successful runs
steps.explain: Steps after a failed step are skipped unless their `if` says otherwise.

steps.title: A Docker build-and-push workflow
body: packages: write                 # allow pushing to ghcr.io
PRs build the image (proving the Dockerfile works) but only `main` pushes it. The tag is the commit SHA, so every image is traceable.

steps.explain: You need the Dockerfile on disk and credentials for the registry before building and pushing.

steps.prompt: Match each expression to its value on a push to `main` of `acme/shop`.
The workflow fails at `docker/login-action` with `denied: installation not allowed to Write organization package`. What is the most likely fix?
steps.explain: `GITHUB_TOKEN` only gets the permissions the workflow declares. Declaring `permissions:` at all sets every unlisted scope to none.

steps.title: Job execution order
prompt: Write `List<string> ExecutionOrder(Dictionary<string, List<string>> needs)` that returns one order in which the jobs could run one at a time.
`needs[job]` lists the jobs it waits for. Whenever several jobs are ready, run the one that comes first **alphabetically** (ordinal).
`{ build: [], lint: [], test: [build], docker: [build, test] }` → `build, lint, test, docker`.
solution: var waiting = needs.ToDictionary(p => p.Key, p => p.Value.Count);
var ready = new SortedSet<string>(waiting.Where(p => p.Value == 0).Select(p => p.Key), StringComparer.Ordinal);
hints: Count how many unfinished dependencies each job has; jobs with zero are ready.
Keep the ready jobs in a `SortedSet<string>`; take `.Min`, then decrement the count of every job that needed it.
